findings.claim: RMDC26 premature/lag/detection for all 1,667 eligible events are set against the in-house giant and Neptune strata, called "the only strata comparable with RMDC26's planetary anomalies". The text says "Alerts come later: ... +6.5 d, against +4.5 d in-house. Detection is lower: 61% (59-64%) ... against 89% and 73% in-house (a different checkpoint on a different simulator, so the difference mixes the two)". REVISION row 10 says "alerts come about two days later".
findings.evidence: The comparison is not like for like in mass ratio. I binned RMDC26's eligible events with the in-house bins (cascade_reduce.Q_REGIMES, lo < q <= hi) using planet_q from rows_full_fspl5s_g08.json (scratch strata.py). Of 1,667 eligible events, 668 (40%) have q <= 1e-4, 826 fall in (1e-4, 1e-3], 149 in (1e-3, 1e-2] and 24 above 1e-2. The in-house scan has only 9 events with q <= 1e-4, and reports none because the stratum is under 20. Recommended checkpoint, F146 only, frozen threshold, per stratum: giant det 79.9% [72.7, 85.5], premature 2/149 = 1.3%, lag +5.0 d (bootstrap 95% 4.5-6.5). Neptune det 65.7% [62.4, 68.9], premature 21/826 = 2.5%, lag +6.5 d [6.0, 7.25]. q <= 1e-4: det 50.7%, lag +7.5 d. In-house, reproduced from validation/cascade_trace.npz (inhouse_strata.py): giant 89.1%, 1.4%, +4.5 d [4.0, 5.5]; Neptune 72.9%, 4.2%, +4.5 d [2.5, 6.5]. Like for like, the detection gap is about 9 and 7 points, not 28 and 12. The giant-stratum lag differs by only 0.5 d and the intervals overlap. So the headline 'later' and part of 'lower' come from RMDC26's many planets with q <= 1e-4, which the parenthesis does not mention. Paper l.1086 gives RMDC26's median q as 1.4e-4 / 1.2e-4, and l.1485-1486 says in-house detection falls at low q. Both are consistent with this being a composition effect.
findings.fix: Stratify the RMDC26 timing numbers by the in-house q bins in cascade_gulls.py (planet_q is in the rows) and add \bmlCg macros for them. Compare giant with giant (80% / 1.3% / +5.0 d vs 89% / 1.4% / +4.5 d) and Neptune with Neptune (66% / 2.5% / +6.5 d vs 73% / 4.2% / +4.5 d). State that 40% of RMDC26's eligible anomalies have q <= 1e-4, a regime the in-house scan samples with 9 events. Add mass-ratio composition to the 'mixes the two' clause, and qualify 'Alerts come later' (clear for Neptune-like and lower-q events; within 0.5 d for giants). Update REVISION.md row 10 ('about two days later', 'detection does not transfer') to match.
findings.verdict_note: I reproduced it from the 82 scan_v2 files (6,000 events, both models) and the planet_q values in rows_full_fspl5s_g08.json, using the Q_REGIMES bins. The 1,667 eligible events split 24 / 149 / 826 / 668 (q<=1e-4 is 40.1%). Recommended checkpoint, F146, frozen threshold, per stratum: giant 79.9% [72.7, 85.5], 2/149 premature, lag +5.0 d (bootstrap 4.5-6.5); Neptune 65.7% [62.4, 68.9], 21/826 premature, +6.5 d (6.0-7.25); q<=1e-4 50.7%, +7.5 d. In-house, reproduced from cascade_trace.npz: giant 89.1% / 1.4% / +4.5 d (4.0-5.5); Neptune 72.9% / 4.2% / +4.5 d (2.5-6.5); only 9 in-house events have q<=1e-4. paper.tex 1402-1409 and the draft mirror at 440-447 read as quoted, and the 09-12b disposition I40 addressed only the checkpoint/simulator confound, not composition. Extra tests make the case stronger. Like for like, giant detection differs at Fisher p=0.035 and Neptune at p=0.35 (not significant). The giant lag difference is not significant (Mann-Whitney p=0.19); the Neptune one is marginal (p=0.05). So most of the headline gaps (6.5 vs 4.5 d, 61% vs 89/73%) come from composition. Major is defensible. Two fixes to the proposed wording: do not call the Neptune lag difference 'clear' (the intervals touch at 6.0-6.5 d), and 'later for lower-q events' cannot be claimed against in-house data (6 in-house lags at q<=1e-4, median +8.5 d).

findings.claim: "The high-cadence season of 3,000 single lenses and 3,000 binaries was revealed ..."; "6.2% of single lenses per simulated event (8.9% weighted by event rate) raise an alert ..."; purity 5% / 21% / 49%.
findings.evidence: The scanned events are the lowest event ids of each class (sample_ids: sorted dense scored ids, first 3,000 / 1,500 / 1,500). Scanned ids equal that set exactly. The paper does not say this, although §gulls:labels does say 'first'. Single-lens ids 3022-30078 cover the bottom 9% of the 3022-306453 range. The sample is not quite representative for the headline variant. Its full-season F146 flag rate with the recommended checkpoint (rows_full_fspl5s_seasons_g08_f146only.json, which equals the scan's last cut to 4 dp for all 6,000 events) is 4.80% [4.1, 5.6], against 5.84% for the other 30,353 dense single lenses (z=2.34, p=0.019). Three-band and calibrated variants are consistent (p=0.32-0.92). Post-stratifying the sample's any-cut alert rate on the last-cut flag gives about 7.1% (weighted 9.9%) for all 33,353 dense single lenses, against the quoted 6.2% (8.9%) (poststrat.py). With that rate, purity at 5% would be about 19% (quoted 21%) and at 22% about 47% (quoted 49%). The 185/3000 binomial interval, 5.4-7.1%, is not quoted.
findings.fix: Say 'the first 3,000 scored single lenses and the first 1,500 of each planetary class (by event id)'. Quote a 95% interval for the single-lens alert rate. Either add the post-stratified (full-population) estimate or note that the sample's full-season single-lens flag rate is about 1 point below the population's, so burden and purity are slightly optimistic.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced exactly. For each class the scanned ids equal sorted(dense scored ids)[:3000/1500/1500]. The single-lens sample spans ids 3022-30078 of a 3022-306453 range. In rows_full_fspl5s_seasons_g08_f146only.json (which matches the scan's last cut within 1e-4 for all 6,000), the sample flags 4.80% [4.09, 5.62] against 5.84% for the other 30,353 (z=2.34, p=0.019). Three-band and calibrated tests give p=0.32-0.92. Post-stratified on the last-cut flag, the any-cut alert rate is 7.10% (9.91% weighted), against 6.17% (8.91%). Rerunning the reducer's purity formula with those rates gives 18.9% at 5% (quoted 21%) and 47.3% at 22% (quoted 49%). The Wilson interval for 185/3000 is 5.36-7.08%. The non-representativeness evidence is marginal: only one of four variants is significant, and not after a 4-way correction. The planetary samples also lean flaggable (1S2L 36.3% vs 34.0%, p=0.08), which pushes purity the same optimistic way. The proposed fix (state 'first by id', add an interval, note the lean) is the right size. Minor.

findings.evidence:
ef6b0bd (2026-07-28) changed the t0 re-pad from `setdefault` to an unconditional assignment. That came after the 2026-07-22 suite, which aws/ud_gentest2.sh generated with pipeline/sim_v5. Whenever an out-of-range override is active, HEAD now uses the redrawn t0 for every event that has a tE: the swept class and the PSPL/NonPSPL context events alike. The July code drew the same number and threw it away.

Method: I generated shard 0 of each quoted tier with sim_v5 at e25e4d6 (run in scratch) and matched events against the cached regenerated subset in stress_local_work.
- Identical: natural 7516/7516, planetary 6869/6869, oor_flat_faint 7952/7952.
- Different: oor_np_widesep shares 2248/4088 events, oor_per_longp 2284/4106, oor_pspl_shortte 508/4116.
- Cause confirmed: HEAD with that one line changed back to setdefault reproduces the July shard exactly (4116/4116, labels equal). Unmodified HEAD reproduces the cache exactly (4121/4121).

For the sub-day tier the population itself differs, not only the realisation:
- Generated sub-day single lenses with t0 outside the season: 20.5% under the July generator (shards 0-3), 0.6% in the regenerated subset.
- PSPL/Flat label fractions: July 0.148/0.594, suite 0.1475/0.5907, regenerated 0.181/0.559.
- Weighted demoted-binary share of the PSPL label: July 43.1%, regenerated 37.5% (the quoted 38%).

I scored the July shortte shards with HEAD's pipeline.cache and pipeline.evaluate (inference only):
- Stage-5 PSPL recall 0.532 (suite 0.524; the regenerated subset's 0.484 is what creates most of the stage-5 subset-vs-suite gap on this row).
- Released model PSPL recall 0.564 (Table: 0.521).
- Single lenses, released: 0.285 PSPL, 69% called anomalies, 35% above the frozen threshold (paper: 0.274 / 71% / 37%).
- Single lenses, stage 5: 0.230 / 53% / 20% (paper: 0.215 / 55% / 21%).

Every directional statement still holds. But the numbers attributed to the set's population are off by 0.01-0.05, and by 5 points for the demoted share.
findings.fix: Under --legacy-oor-mix, or a new --legacy-t0-pad, restore the July behaviour: draw the re-pad t0 but keep the original. Then regenerate the three override tiers (widesep, per_longp, shortte), rescore them with stress_rescore_local.py and rebuild the macros. Alternatively, drop 'bit for bit'/'exactly' from the code and docs, and say in the paper, table caption and PROVENANCE that these tiers were generated with the corrected t0 padding. They are then a different realisation of the suite, and a different population for sub-day timescales, so the 38% should not be attributed to the full set.
findings.verdict_note:
Reproduced in scratch/verify4/adv_code with a git-archive copy of e25e4d6 pipeline/sim_v5, HEAD, and HEAD with line 337 of assemble.py set back to setdefault.

Shard-level results:
- Unmodified HEAD with --legacy-oor-mix matches the cached subset exactly for shard 0 of all six tiers.
- HEAD with setdefault matches sim_v5 exactly.
- Events shared between sim_v5 and the cache: shortte 508/4116, widesep 2249/4088 (the finding says 2248; the difference is key rounding), longp 2284/4106. Natural, planetary and faint shards are identical.

Population:
- sim_v5 shortte shards 0-3: PSPL/Flat 0.1479/0.5940. Suite: 0.1475/0.5907. Regenerated subset: 0.1814/0.5585 (z=+12).
- All 20 suite shards with sim_v5: 12,149 PSPL labels (suite 12,122). HEAD gives 14,722.
- Sub-day single lenses with t0 outside the season: 20.55% under sim_v5, 0.63% in the subset.

Scoring the July-generator shards with HEAD's evaluate reproduces every quoted number:
- Stage 5: PSPL 0.532; single lenses 0.230 / 53.2% / 19.8%.
- Released: PSPL 0.564; single lenses 0.285 / 69.3% / 35.3%.

Two refinements:
1. Over all 20 shards the suite-population demoted share is 42.2%; 43.1% was the four-shard value. The paper's 38% (line 792, PROVENANCE, REVISION row 23) is therefore about 4 points low, not 5.
2. The first fix alone will not give 'bit for bit'. Even e25e4d6's sim_v5 does not reproduce the suite's wide-separation population: 296 NonPSPL labels over 20 shards (HEAD 286) against the suite's 438; subset 0.0037 against 0.0053. That gap is not caused by t0 and its cause is unknown. Use the disclosure fix: drop 'bit for bit'/'exactly', and call the override tiers a new realisation (for sub-day tE, a different population), with the 38% attributed to the subset or about 42% quoted for the suite. Directional statements hold. Major is defensible because the reproducibility claim is false.

findings.fix: Add `!validation/referee_round_archive/` and `!validation/referee_round_archive/*` exceptions to .gitignore, or force-add the files, and commit the 25 MB archive. Otherwise remove the 'archived/committed' claims from paper.tex, PROVENANCE, CHANGELOG and REVISION, and reopen I29.
findings.verdict_note:
HEAD and origin/main are both 943b171.

findings.claim: "A base model was trained from scratch on 540,952 natural-prior events with AdamW (learning rate 3x10^-4, weight decay 0.01, batch size 512)". The 12b critic-#2 disposition, CHANGELOG:39-40 and REVISION row 23 also say the recipe now comes "from the stage logs".
findings.evidence: The base log (v5runs/train_20260721_0003.log) records only 'epochs=18 batch=512' and gives no learning rate. The base run's own optimizer and scheduler state is in v5runs/binml_v5_base.pt.last. Its history matches the log exactly (NonPSPL F1 0.682/0.821/0.824/0.844/0.799/0.589; best 0.8440 at epoch 3, the same value as binml_v5_base.pt). It shows param_groups max_lr=0.0004, initial_lr=1.6e-05 (=4e-4/25) and weight_decay 0.01. findings.fix: Change the base rate to 4x10^-4 (the peak of a one-cycle schedule). Correct the 12b critic-#2 disposition, CHANGELOG and REVISION row 23, which list 3e-4 'from the stage logs'. Consider writing the recipe numbers into the canonical_numbers.json infra block from the .last optimizer states, with a check.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced. v5runs/binml_v5_base.pt.last: param_groups max_lr=0.0004, initial_lr=1.6e-05, wd=0.01. OneCycle total_steps is 19,026 (18 x 1,057), warm-up ends at step 2,852.9 and last_epoch is 6,342. The history matches train_20260721_0003.log (best 0.84403 at ep 3). The log has only 'epochs=18 batch=512' and no LR, and no launch command with 4e-4 survives anywhere in the workspace. The stage-era train_v5.py (ef216e2) passes max_lr=args.lr unscaled, so the base run was launched at 4e-4, and 3e-4 is only the default. The other stages match the text: 1.2e-4 (8,456 steps), 3e-5 (6,270), 5e-5 (13,326 for stages 4-5, 23,832 for stage 6). The LR at the kept epoch 3 is about 3.93e-4. findings.claim: "stage 6 applied the truncation relabelling to every class"
findings.evidence: stage6_20260726_0025.log: 'FIX 1: truncation relabel now uses t_anom -> Flat->PSPL->NonPSPL cascade (no premature binary flags)'; cache 'ALL 211,906 NonPSPL have t_anom'. The stage-3-era code (git show ef216e2:pipeline/sim_v5/train_v5.py, _apply_truncation) already relabels truncated single and binary lenses to Flat by visible PSPL amplitude, and eruptives by start time. Stage 5 (log FIX 1) extended the floor to periodic classes. What stage 6 added is the binary-onset rule (binary -> PSPL before t_anom), which is the cascade that section 4 evaluates. The appendix never says when that mechanism entered training.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'stage 6 relabelled truncated binaries as PSPL until their recorded anomaly onset (the cascade of Sec. cascade) and added pools that ...'.
findings.verdict_note: The stage-3-era _apply_truncation (ef216e2) already relabelled truncated PSPL/NonPSPL to Flat by visible PSPL amplitude, and eruptives by t_start. The stage-5/6 code (e25e4d6) added the periodic range-traversed amplitude, which the stage 5 log calls FIX 1. Stage 6's new element is the t_anom rule (NonPSPL -> PSPL before onset; stage 6 log FIX 1). So 'stage 6 applied the truncation relabelling to every class' misattributes the change, and the appendix never says when the onset cascade entered training. Minor.

findings.claim: The recipe gives single learning rates per stage, calls the model 'the last of six warm-started stages', and for the fine-tunes gives only learning rates ('colour-calibration 5e-5, RMDC26 1e-4').
findings.evidence: (a) Every stage uses OneCycleLR (pipeline/train.py:776-777; already in ef216e2). The quoted rates are peaks, reached after a 15% warm-up from lr/25, followed by a cosine anneal to about 1e-10 with beta1 cycling (all visible in the .last scheduler states). gaps.target: paper/paper.tex:593-595, 628-631 and 716-723 at 9c04593 (Sec. results and Fig. plane), which describe where the released model misses detectable anomalies
gaps.why: None of the six slices looked at Sec. results this round. These three passages are hand-written prose with no macro or guard behind them, and they are the paper's only account of where the in-distribution failures sit. They also set up the stress section, which presents wide separation as an out-of-range failure.
gaps.result:
CONFIRMED DEFECT. (1) Lines 594-595 say the NonPSPL->PSPL misses are 'weak but detectable anomalies ... concentrated at the lowest evidence strengths'. (2) Lines 630-631 say the misses are 'concentrated just above the detectability floor where the anomaly signal is weakest'. (3) Lines 718-720 say conditional recall is 'high across most of the plane ... falls to ~0.5 only in the low-q, low-support corners at log q <~ -4'.

Evidence: my own code on the tracked arrays in paper/results (label, logits, params, dchi2_anomaly, score_nonpspl, test_idx; 360,472 final-test rows; 42,805 detectable anomalies). Of the 2,207 argmax misses, the counts by Delta-chi2_anom bin are:
- 160-500: 378 (17%)
- 500-2k: 397 (18%)
- 2k-10k: 414 (19%)
- 1e4-1e5: 544 (25%)
- >1e5: 474 (21%)
So 47% have Delta-chi2 above 1e4. The median Delta-chi2 of the misses is 6,932.

The dominant driver is separation, not evidence strength. 55% of all misses and 56% of the 2,093 NonPSPL->PSPL confusions are binaries with s > 2.92 (log s > 0.466, the top separation bin of the prior), although these are only 11% of detectable anomalies. Their miss rate is 22-30% in every Delta-chi2 bin; for s < 2.92 it is 11.6% at 160-500 and 0.4% above 1e5. Wide stellar-ratio binaries (s > 2.92, q > 0.01; 4,537 events) are recovered at 0.733 (argmax) and 0.592 at the frozen threshold, against 0.981 and 0.931 at s < 2.92. At the operating threshold 36% of the 5,179 misses are wide, and the misses are spread evenly across the Delta-chi2 bins (21/21/21/21/16%).

The efficiency-plane artifact itself (metrics.json) has conditional recall 0.715 and 0.690 in the two top-right cells (log q -1 to 0, log s 0.47-0.70), with effective detectable support of 1,298 and 2,595. These are among the best-populated cells in the plane, not low-support corners, and they are visible in the rendered Fig. 8.

The wide-separation weakness therefore starts inside the natural prior, despite stage 6's s = 3-8 pool, and the stress sweep at s = 5-12 extends it. No doc or verification round mentions it.

Fix: state the two sources of misses:
- near-floor anomalies (for s < 3);
- wide-separation binaries, missed about a quarter of the time whatever their strength, which make up about 55% of misses.
